NEVER shipped as a table: armed only by the scripted URL parameter ?ballreturn=TEST-shallow-merge on the scripted pin table.

doc.notes: Same served pockets, support, resistance and tray as TEST-synthetic-wire-slide; only the two entry runways differ: each runs from its side cup to a single mid vertex and then into the trunk head, so the last edge meets the trunk at 17.1° in plan instead of 76.0°. At that angle the two approaches stay within one ball diameter of each other for 45 mm past the station the merge law used to pick, so the yield station is pushed 44.9 mm beyond the one-diameter minimum; below 15.05° (measured on this family) no station within the two-diameter cap is clear and the track is REFUSED. Geometry values are TEST reads chosen from the table's own dimensions with stated clearances; nothing here is a claim about any real slide.

provenance.source: WPA Equipment Specifications §16, 2 1/4 in pool ball (crates/pool-core default r 0.028575)

PROXY: the kernel default class (params.rs ClothPreset::default, u_r 0.010 — Waldron stimpmeter roll-out, a first-hand cloth measurement) stands in for the unmeasured steel-wire class. On the twin rail the effective coefficient is (7/5)(r/ρ)·u_r = 1.4 × 1.322 × 0.010 = 0.0185 (track.js resistCoeff); drain margin at the shallowest edge: sin θ 0.0436 vs 0.0185.

research.md R5 / the brief's 'inelastic arrival' and the owner's 「一个接一个堆」: arriving balls share a common velocity with the group they touch, the tray wall is infinite mass. A modelling decision, NOT a measurement — no ball-on-ball impact in a return tray has been captured in this repo; a measured e would enter through this block and a runtime law change (spec §7).
